label: STOPP D9
title: Benzodiazepine for agitation or psychotic symptoms of dementia
statement: Benzodiazepines for agitated behaviour or psychotic symptoms of dementia (no evidence of efficacy).

source.document: O'Mahony D, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632, Appendix 1 (corrected supplementary file; NHS Somerset copy used for text, sentence-identical to the earlier parse)
source.citation: O'Mahony D, Cherubini A, Guiteras AR, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632. doi:10.1007/s41999-023-00777-y

plain_summary: A benzodiazepine (a sedating anxiety or sleep medicine) given to a person with dementia for agitated behaviour or psychotic symptoms has no proven benefit and can cause harm.

medicine_groups.name: Benzodiazepines
medicine_groups.note: Tablets, capsules, liquids and injections count. Z-drugs such as zolpidem and zopiclone are not benzodiazepines and do not count. Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too.

needs_facts.what: Reason for this benzodiazepine in relation to dementia
needs_facts.meets: A recorded diagnosis of dementia with agitation or psychotic symptoms due to dementia documented as the reason for this benzodiazepine.

options.words: Prescribed for agitation or psychotic symptoms due to dementia
A clinical assessment ruled out dementia

rule_for_models: Apply this rule only to people aged 65 years or older. If age is unknown, confirm it before reporting a STOPP finding. Suspect a finding when a Group A benzodiazepine is supplied and the record links that prescription to agitation or psychotic symptoms due to dementia. Cite the supply and the evidence linking it to the symptom and diagnosis. A documented indication solely for another reason or an explicit clinical assessment that the person does not have dementia gives no finding. A normal cognitive screen alone leaves dementia status unresolved. If a Group A benzodiazepine is supplied and neither exclusion applies, report a possible finding when dementia or the indication is unknown and name the missing information.
cannot_be_seen: Whether the person really has dementia if no diagnosis is recorded, what the benzodiazepine was prescribed for (agitation, anxiety, sleep or another reason), and any benzodiazepine given in hospital or a care home.
ask_the_gp: A review of whether the benzodiazepine is needed for this person with dementia, and of non-drug options for the behaviour.
